title: mcp-claude-hooks Architecture
description: Bus-centric architecture. Schema is the single source of truth. Bus is the core — all modules register handlers on bus. All adapters are interchangeable I/O shells. There is only ONE process, ONE bus, ONE engine. Adapters (MCP/CLI/SSE/hook) are transport skins.

Layer.description: Architectural layer. core=runtime infrastructure (bus+schema2object+errors, direct calls OK). modules=generic capabilities (bus only, never import each other). extends=application compositions (compose modules for specific scenarios). adapters=I/O skins (stdio/sse/cli/daemon).

ImportSource.description: core: node-stdlib + core-direct (direct calls within core are legal). modules: bus-only (no cross-module import). extends: bus-only + may declare children. adapters: injection (receives core via injection, never imports modules).

CoreComponent.description: Core = runtime infrastructure. Always present. Cannot unload. Components communicate via direct function calls — bus is not required within core. Core provides: bus, schema2object (ObjectTree+Loader), errors, log, module loader.

x-constraint.const: Direct function calls within core are legal. Core never goes through bus.
x-constraint.description: Core is the runtime — it cannot depend on what it provides.

FeatureContract.description: Features are engine plugins — named dynamic-value computers invoked after rule match. Not bus handlers. Not modules. Sync execution only: returns value immediately, passed to handler as featureResult.

name.description: Registry key. Referenced by rule.feature field.

returns.description: Feature return type. Engine passes result to handler as featureResult parameter.

BusMessage.description: Semantic definition of a bus message. Bus is request-response only: one handler per event via bus.handle(), caller awaits result via bus.send(). No pub/sub, no fire-and-forget.

pattern.description: handle = exactly one handler registered via bus.handle(). bus.send() calls handler and returns result. No handler = throw.

correlation.description: request-response: caller awaits reply (bus.send returns result).

owner.description: Which module registers the handler for this event (handle pattern only).

DependencyRule.description: Strict layering rules. Reverse dependency = bug. Module-to-module direct import = bug.

DependencyRules.description: Complete dependency rule set. Validated by dependency-cruiser.
x-invariants: core: direct function calls within core are legal — core never goes through bus
modules: never import each other — all inter-module communication via bus.send()
modules: may import core (schema2object, errors) directly
extends: compose modules for specific scenarios — communicate via bus
adapters: receive core via injection — never import modules directly
main.mjs: reads config.json, calls boot(), routes to adapter — nothing hardwired

BusEventName.description: Bus event names follow namespace:action pattern

EventDeclaration.description: One event in a module's contract. Mirrors jster module.schema.json handles[]/listens[]/emits[] structure.

payload.description: JSON Schema Draft-07 shape of the payload. Used for ObjectTree construction and MCP tool generation.

ModuleContract.description: Module = one schema file + one code file. Schema declares identity and event contract. Code implements setup(bus, config) → teardown. Modules never import each other — bus only. Module may import core (schema2object, errors) directly.

version.description: Semver. Declared as const in module schema.

depends.description: Module names that must load before this one. Boot toposorts automatically.

handles.description: Events this module handles (one handler per event, registered via bus.handle).

listens.description: Events this module observes (bus.on — fire-and-forget, no reply).

emits.description: Events this module emits (bus.emit). Declared for documentation and wiring.

x-decision.description: Why this module exists as a separate unit

AdapterContract.description: Adapters are pure I/O skins. One job: translate external protocol into core's language (core.handle / bus.send). They receive core via injection — never import L1 or L2 directly. main.mjs is the core; adapters are interchangeable shells.

injection.description: How the adapter receives its execution context — never via direct import

x-argv-scope.description: For cli adapter only. Defines which argv commands this adapter owns.

CommandPattern.description: All external inputs are Commands. Each adapter translates its protocol into a Command and submits to core.handle(). This is the Command Pattern — the request itself is an object, decoupled from execution. Three entry points, one handler interface.

translation.description: How external input becomes a Command

entry_points.x-invariant: Every adapter calls exactly one handle interface. No adapter calls two.

x-gap.const: argv not yet formally translated to Command — stop/status/reload live in main.mjs if/else. Needs refactor: ArgvAdapter → Command → core.handle().
x-gap.description: Current deviation from full Command Pattern compliance.

CliAdapterScope.description: cli adapter is the unified argv entry point. All external CLI interactions — daemon control, boot mode selection, and interactive tool invocation — go through cli adapter. main.mjs only decides: is this hook mode (piped stdin) or CLI mode?

daemon_commands.description: Commands that talk to daemon process directly — no boot required.

boot_flags.description: Flags that influence boot mode selection.

interactive_commands.description: Commands that boot core then invoke tools: 'cli <category> [action] [key=value...]'

ExtendContract.description: Extends compose modules into specific application scenarios. An extend knows the business context. It may declare child modules. config.json lists root extends only — children self-declare in schema. Internal communication via object module + fn call. Only external boundary uses bus.

composes.description: Module names this extend depends on and composes together.

children.description: Child modules declared in this extend's schema. Loaded as part of this extend.

internal_pattern.description: Internal communication pattern. object-module-fn = createX(config) → { methods }, direct fn calls between children. bus = children register on bus. Default is object-module-fn — bus only at external boundary.

bus_surface.description: Bus events exposed at external boundary. Internal fn calls are invisible to bus.

HookMatchStrategy.description: match = ObjectTree(event, schema) succeeds. match_bash = parse command nodes, ObjectTree(cmd, schema) any succeeds. No match field = always match.

MergePolicy.description: When multiple rules match the same event, merge by priority.

priority_order.description: deny > ask > allow > context. All matched rules tagged in reason.

reason_format.description: Each matched rule contributes one tagged segment to the merged reason string

ProgressiveDisclosure.description: L1/L2/L3 dispatch model. Do not merge all action params into L1. Show progressively.

L1.description: Tool list call. Return minimal schema — action enum and format only.

L2.const: args + example + inputSchema on validation error
L2.description: No action provided, or validation failed. Return full args with example.

L3.description: Valid input received. Execute and return result.

DataFlow.description: Cross-module operations go through bus events. Within extends, children use fn calls.

steps.description: Ordered sequence of bus events and transform steps

BootStrategy.description: How main.mjs decides which runtime path to take. One entry point, multiple modes. Daemon-first: every mode attempts daemon socket before cold start. Module set loaded is determined by mode — not hardwired.

entry.description: Only entry point. No other file is executed directly.

decision_tree.description: Ordered checks that determine the boot mode. First match wins.

condition.description: Boolean condition on argv + stdin state

daemon_first.description: Daemon-first rule: every mode that needs core first checks for a running daemon socket. If found, wrap as proxy core (no module loading). Only cold-start if no daemon.

core_components.description: Runtime infrastructure. Always present. Cannot unload. Direct function calls within core are legal. Provides: bus, schema2object, errors, log, module loader.

extends.description: Application compositions. Each extend assembles modules for a specific scenario (e.g. mcp-server, hook-engine). config.json lists root extends only.

modules.description: Business logic modules. Each registers handlers on bus via setup(bus, config).

adapters.description: Pure I/O adapters. Interchangeable transport skins.

features.description: Engine plugins. Invoked after rule match when rule.feature is set. Not bus handlers — direct function calls from engine.

bus_messages.description: All named bus messages with their semantic pattern (handle vs send) and correlation type.

command_pattern.description: Three entry points (argv/JSON-RPC/stdin), one handle interface. Command Pattern.

cli_adapter_scope.description: Defines the boundary of cli adapter as the unified argv entry point.

data_flows.description: Named data flows through the system

design_decisions.description: Key architectural decisions with rationale. Equivalent to ADRs.
x-decisions: Single log file (logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log): foundation/log-file.mjs is shared primitive. main.mjs writes pre-bus; server/log.mjs writes post-bus. Same format, one file.
run/ for runtime state: hook-state.json, hook.pid, hook.sock, daemon.err all live in run/. logs/ is append-only log output only.
bash-compat name field: toCommand() must never assign name:undefined. Use conditional assignment — ObjectTree required check sees undefined key as present.
Daemon restart = fork new → SIGTERM old. NEVER process.exit() in daemon mode — that kills the daemon with no replacement. New daemon's startDaemon() cleans stale pidfile+socket automatically.
__HOOKS_DAEMON_CHILD env var: set by fork parent, preserved for entire daemon lifetime. admin:restart uses it to detect daemon mode. main.mjs no longer deletes it after fork guard.
Daemon stderr capture: fork with stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe','ipc'], pipe stdout+stderr to run/daemon.err. Makes daemon crashes visible without console access.

Hooks encapsulation: hook.mjs is root extend. Internal children (rules, features, engine, handles) use object module + fn call. Bus surface: hooks:process-event (engine entry) + engine:reload (reload trigger → rules.reload()). config.json mounts hook.schema.json as single leaf node.

Object module pattern: createX(config) → { methods }. Engine receives rules/features via dependency injection. Handlers receive features ref as parameter. No internal bus, no cross-import between children.
Handler ObjectTree-first: new ObjectTree({}, schema.responseSchema, loader) → operate properties → return ObjectTree. Engine calls .$toDict() at exit. Handlers never construct plain objects.

Observability: every object module and every non-trivial fn must emit bus.send('log', ...) at debug level. bus is infra — internal fn-call pattern does not prohibit bus log. Log prefix = module:fn (e.g. engine:match, handle:PreToolUse, match:validate, state:hasFired, merge:priority, feature:execute). hook.mjs passes bus to createEngine; engine passes log fn to handler payload; hook-match/state/merger/features receive bus or log fn at creation.

boot_strategy.description: Defines how main.mjs decides which runtime path to take. Single entry, multiple modes, daemon-first for all modes that need core.

x-constraint-targets.bus_events: ESLint no-restricted-imports or custom lint rule
x-constraint-targets.module_contract: static analysis: every project/modules/*.mjs must export setup(bus)
x-constraint-targets.adapter_contract: static analysis: adapters/*.mjs must not import from foundation/ or server/

x-entry-points.description: main.mjs is the only entry point. Routes by argv and stdin state. Every mode that needs core applies daemon-first: try unix socket proxy, cold-start only if no daemon. Module set loaded is determined by mode — see boot_strategy.modes.
x-entry-points.decision_summary: hook (piped stdin) → daemon-proxy|cold-start → runHook → exit; daemon-control: stop/status → direct IPC, reload/restart → daemon socket tools/call; daemon (--daemon flag) → full boot + socket; cli (cli subcommand) → daemon-proxy|cold-start → runCLI; mcp-stdio (default) → daemon-proxy|cold-start → startStdio
modes: main.mjs --daemon                → daemon mode: fork + full boot
main.mjs stop                    → daemon-control: IPC, no boot
main.mjs status                  → daemon-control: IPC, no boot
main.mjs reload                  → daemon-control: daemon socket → tools/call hooks_admin:reload
main.mjs restart                 → daemon-control: daemon socket → tools/call hooks_admin:restart
admin:restart (daemon internal)   → fork new daemon + SIGTERM self (never process.exit)
main.mjs cli <category> [action] → cli mode: daemon-proxy or cold-start
echo event | main.mjs            → hook mode: daemon-proxy or cold-start → exit

x-foundation.description: This system is built on jster as the underlying runtime. jster provides: bus (dual-layer emit/send), module loader (toposort, hot-plug), schema2object (ObjectTree+Loader+KVO), core infrastructure. All development posture follows jster conventions.
x-dev-posture: Schema FIRST — write <name>.schema.json before <name>.mjs. Schema IS the contract.
config.json IS a Schema — not a data file. default values ARE runtime config. new ObjectTree({}, configSchema) extracts all defaults as live object.
Module = schema + code. One directory, two files: <name>.schema.json + <name>.mjs.
setup(bus, config) → teardown(). Every module exports setup, returns teardown.
handles/listens/emits declared in schema — these are the observable contract, not implementation details.
depends[] drives boot order — toposort is automatic, no manual ordering.
bus.send() replaces all direct function calls between modules — same sync semantics, adds observability. bus is request-response only: one handler per event, no pub/sub.
Core components (bus, schema2object) may be imported directly — they are infrastructure, not modules.
Adapters receive core via injection — never import modules or extends directly.

x-config-schema.description: config.json is a JSON Schema, not a data file. This is a jster core invariant.
x-config-schema.pattern: new ObjectTree({}, configSchema, loader) extracts all defaults as a live ObjectTree.
x-config-schema.consequence: Adding a new config value = add it to config.json schema with a default. Code reads it as config.property — no parsing, no env wrangling.

example.code: config.logLevel  // 'info' — live ObjectTree getter, validated at construction

x-adapter-pattern.description: All adapters follow the same pattern: external protocol → core.handle(). main.mjs is core. Adapters are skins.
x-adapter-pattern.x-decision: cli adapter owns ALL argv parsing. stop/status/reload/restart are daemon-control commands. reload/restart go through daemon socket → tools/call (same path as MCP). stop/status are direct IPC (no boot). main.mjs only distinguishes: hook mode (piped stdin) vs everything else (cli adapter).

x-core-invariants: ONE process, ONE bus, ONE engine
main.mjs is the ONLY entry point — no other file is executed directly
Daemon-first: every mode that needs core tries daemon socket before cold-start
Module set is mode-specific — hook loads engine+rules only; mcp/daemon/cli load full set
Cross-module operations go through bus events. Within an extend, children use object module + fn call (no bus). Extends expose minimal bus surface at boundary.
Schema is the single source of truth
Rules ARE JSON Schema Draft-07 documents — matching = ObjectTree construction succeeds
HSO schema properties determine action→field mapping — zero hardcoded event names
Adapter receives core via injection — never via direct import
Hook fallback: daemon down → cold start engine in-process; exit immediately after response
Single log file: logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log — text format. foundation/log-file.mjs is the shared write primitive used by main.mjs (pre-bus) and server/log.mjs (post-bus). No JSONL, no separate audit file.
Runtime state in run/: hook-state.json, hook.pid, hook.sock, daemon.err. Not in logs/.

One event, one handler: every hooks/*.json event schema MUST have a dedicated handler in handles/{EventName}.mjs. Handler reads the event's response schema — no default fallback for known events. default.mjs is only for truly unknown events. Each handler is the minimal processing unit, instantiated by its own event schema.

Handler reads event schema for full capability: response properties (decision, stopReason, suppressOutput), HSO type ($ref or anyOf), and event-specific input fields. A generic default handler loses event-specific capabilities.

One tool action, one handle: each tools.json action maps to exactly one bus.handle(). Composition = handler internally calls bus.send() to other handles. mcp.mjs wiring layer does pure bus.handle(event, fn) binding only — no orchestration logic. This ensures internal triggers (rules:changed → hooks_admin:reload) and external triggers (MCP tools/call → hooks_admin:reload) walk the same code path.

Reload single path: all reload triggers (CLI, MCP tool, CRUD rules:changed, SIGHUP) converge to hooks_admin:reload. admin.reload() internally calls bus.send('engine:reload') + bus.send('hooks_rules:reload'). engine:reload is handled by hook.mjs → rules.reload() (engine match data). hooks_rules:reload reloads handler cache.
